classification.label: introduced by the filter script
classification.statement: The 5,911 NULL-date rows are exactly the rows sourced from file2 (momentum_scan_2025.parquet), which never had a 'date' column at all - it has 'event_date' instead. filter_events_power_law.py's pd.concat([df1, df2], ignore_index=True) (line 22) is a column-union concat; it reconciles 'volume'->'event_volume' explicitly (lines 15-16) but performs no equivalent reconciliation of 'date'<->'event_date'. Every file2-sourced row therefore gets date=NaN by construction of the concat, not from any NULL value present in a source file.
classification.why_not_a: Category (a) would mean the scan inputs already carried NULL in an existing 'date' field. That is not what happens: file2 has no 'date' field to be NULL in - the field is absent from its schema entirely. The NULL is manufactured by the union-concat at script line 22, which is squarely the filter script's doing.
classification.why_not_c: The evidence is fully determinable and disjoint/exhaustive (see evidence below), so (c) does not apply.

perfect_partition_check.query: SELECT date IS NULL, COUNT(*), COUNT(event_date) FROM momentum_events GROUP BY 1
perfect_partition_check.interpretation: date IS NULL and event_date IS NOT NULL are the same 5,911 rows, and date IS NOT NULL and event_date IS NULL are the same 17,357 rows. The partition is perfect and disjoint - direct confirmation that 'date' and 'event_date' are mutually-exclusive artifacts of which input file a row came from, not independent fields.

schema_origin.script_reconciliation: filter_events_power_law.py:15-16 renames file1's 'volume' to 'event_volume' - the only schema reconciliation performed between the two files. No equivalent step exists for date/event_date.

row_arithmetic.note: All 5,911 NULL-date rows in momentum_events are file2-sourced rows that additionally survived the q05 volume-floor filter (script line 62). 39 of the 5,950 raw file2 rows were dropped by that filter, same mechanism as any other row - see refit_comparison.json (T2).

none_date_lookup_cross_reference.statement: All 114 folders whose name contains the literal string 'None' as the date token resolve to momentum_events rows with a NULL date column (113 matched cleanly to a single NULL-date row, 1 matched multiple NULL-date rows ambiguously - ticker had >1 NULL-date event, folder-name momentum alone did not disambiguate). Zero matched a valid-date row. The 114 literal-None folders are a strict subset of the 5,911 NULL-date rows (114/5,911 = 1.93%) - they are the subset of file2-sourced events for which the folder-naming step (collect_massive_data.py:126, date_str = str(row.date)) stringified the missing date as the literal text 'None' rather than a blank/NaN token, when building the folder name {ticker}_{date}_{momentum_pct}.

null_vs_dated_comparison.note: Comparable columns only - file1 and file2 have almost entirely disjoint schemas beyond ticker/prev_close/momentum_pct/price_move/event_volume (see schema_split_columns below). Full distribution in chart 01_momentum_pct_by_date_status.html (T6); numbers below are the summary stats behind it, all with n.

momentum_pct.observation: Medians are close (44.41 vs 42.6) but the null-date group's max is ~1,100x the dated group's max (53.8M vs 48.6K), which drags its mean three orders of magnitude above its own median. Not a simple 'same distribution' - see chart 01 for the full ECDF, log-scale, outliers shown per Evidence Standard.

schema_split_columns.note: These columns are populated in exactly one group by construction of which input file a row came from - not a genuine distributional comparison, just confirms the file1/file2 split from T1a.

surprises: market_cap_est and sector are declared columns in file2/momentum_events but are 100% NULL in both groups (0/17357 dated, 0/5911 null-date) - the columns exist but were never populated for any surviving row.

The NULL-date group's momentum_pct has a max of 53,799,900 (%), ~1,100x the dated group's max of 48,557.72 - an extreme outlier or data-quality artifact in file2 that chart 01 will need to show without clipping.
